summary: This note surveys seven book and poetry festivals taking place across the United States from September to November 2023, each in a different city and with its own focus. They range from poetry readings in Springfield to historical fiction in Portland, academic literature in Chicago and world literature in Denver. The note names featured authors, workshops and special events at each festival.
one_line: A guide to seven autumn 2023 US book and poetry festivals, from Springfield to Denver, with their dates, themes and featured authors.
key_facts: The National Poetry Festival in Springfield begins September 5, 2023, runs four days, and features poets such as Elizabeth Harmon and Michael Ondaatje, with workshops, readings and spoken word performances.
The Literary Gala by the Sea takes place September 12-15, 2023 in Monterey, with headliners Angela Davis Roberts and John Green and discussions ranging from climate fiction to modern memoirs.
The Inner City Wordsmith Festival launches September 20, 2023 in New York City as a 10-day event mixing indie bookshops, street poets and emerging fiction writers.
The Inner City Wordsmith Festival features interactive sessions led by author Luis Gomez and 'live writing' challenges orchestrated by Sarah Knight.
The Historical Fiction Forum runs October 4-7, 2023 in Portland, with roundtable discussions, historically themed dinners and a closing costume ball.
Edward Rutherfurd and Philippa Gregory are notable authors at The Historical Fiction Forum, sharing the research behind their narratives.
The Grand Book and Arts Carnival runs October 14-21, 2023 in San Antonio as an eight-day festival combining visual arts and literature, described as the biggest collective event of the season.
Olivia Parker, a painter and children's book author, hosts 'Art in Storytelling' workshops at the Grand Book and Arts Carnival, which also introduces its first 'Live Literary Mural' project.
The Campus Literary Festival takes place October 25-27, 2023 on university grounds in Chicago, with panels on 'The Evolution of the English Language' and 'Literary Criticism in the 21st Century'.
Dr. James Conrad, a professor and literary critic, holds a masterclass on 'Interpreting Postmodern Literature' at the Campus Literary Festival.
The Biannual World Literature Fair is in Denver from November 2-5, 2023, celebrating translations and international works, including 'The Labyrinth of Solitude' and 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'.
The Biannual World Literature Fair offers multilingual readings and a special pavilion dedicated to language diversity.
